label: late original-phase input of n/c/f/s/w/q/l in sequences starting with p/i/g/j/o/m/t/3
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at the delimiter or during copying, and never at t=0 or 1. The firing rate climbs with position: 0.3% at t=2 up to 13.7% at orig_idx 8, and about half the mass is on the last original token (to_go=0), so long sequences (L=8,9) carry most of it. The input token matters a lot: n, c and f (5-7x lift, about 63% of the mass), then s, w, q and l. The first token of the sequence matters too: p, i, g, j, o, m, t and 3 have 2.4-3.8x lift, and sequences starting with q, n, y or r give many false positives. It usually fires on the first occurrence of the input token (86% of the mass). The behaviour looks like a graded hidden-state readout, so the boolean predicate is imprecise: dev precision is about 0.37, recall 0.63 and mass recall 0.70. The strongest activations sit on n/c/f in the last 1-2 original positions, often after earlier s/c/f/n tokens.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: n, c, f, s, w, q; least: h, m, u, 2) and the first original token (most: p, i, g, j, o, m; least: l, s, c, n); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, t=7, L=9 & t=7.
